newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hanwha Group prepares for restructuring.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hanwha Group prepares for restructuring.

text.p: South Korea's Hanwha Group said on Wednesday it was preparing a restructuring plan aimed at improving its competitiveness.
"We'll announce a complete set of restructuring plans on our various business lines by the end of this year," said a group spokesman.
Hanwha, the nation's ninth largest conglomerate with 32 affiliates, would cut unprofitable business lines and focus on money-making sectors, he said.
Hanwha currently focuses on energy affiliates -- Hanwha Energy Co Ltd, and Hanwha Chemical Corp.
The group, for example, was considering selling off the unprofitable lubricant division of Hanwha Energy, he said.
Analysts said the group's move stemmed from financial pressures. The group strongly denied any financial problems.
"Our cash flow is very smooth," the spokesman said. "We don't have all of our funds stuck in one business area like the troubled Kia and Hanbo groups. We haven't had a major investment since 1990."
Hanwha Group posted a net loss of 164.9 billion won in 1996 on a turnover of 9.6 trillion. The spokesman blamed the economic downturn for the group's loss.

The group's ratio of debt-to-shareholders' equity stood at 778 percent at the end of last year, compared with Kia Group's 523 percent and Ssangyong Group's 409 percent, according to the Office of Bank Supervision.
"Hanwha's cash flow situation is terrible," said Lee Sang-koo, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
"It has no cash cow among its affiliates. The group needs restructuring to cut out loss-making businesses."
